findings.claim: mode() returns the maximum value (last element after numeric sort) instead of the most frequently occurring value; e.g. mode([1,2,2,3]) returns 3 but the mode is 2, and mode([5,1,1]) returns 5 but the mode is 1.
findings.requiredAction: Implement mode by counting value frequencies and returning the value with the highest count (with a defined tie-breaking rule), not by returning the maximum.

findings.claim: mode() sorts the caller's array in place via values.sort(...), mutating its input; the neighboring median() explicitly copies with [...values].sort(...) to avoid this side effect.
findings.requiredAction: Avoid mutating the input: operate on a copy (e.g. [...values]) or compute frequencies without sorting, matching the non-mutating behavior of median().

findings.claim: The new mode() function has no test coverage; test/stats.test.js imports only mean and median, so the incorrect implementation passes the suite undetected.
findings.requiredAction: Add tests for mode() covering typical input (repeated values), the empty-array case, and input-array non-mutation.

findings.claim: The new mode() implementation still has no test coverage; test/stats.test.js imports only mean and median, so a regression in mode() would pass the suite undetected. (The constraint forbidding test-file modification prevented addressing this in the fix.)
findings.requiredAction: Add tests for mode() (e.g. mode([1,2,2,3]) === 2, mode([5,1,1]) === 1, tie-breaking, and input-array immutability) when test modifications are permitted.
